ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, the perpendicular bisector DM of side AC intersects AC at D, and the perpendicular bisector EN of side CB intersects BC at E. DM and EN intersect at point F. If $\angle MFN=70^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle MCN$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that MD$\perp$AC and NE$\perp$BC, \\
it follows that $\angle ACB=180^\circ-\angle MFN=110^\circ$, \\
which leads to $\angle A+\angle B=70^\circ$, \\
Given MA=MC and NB=NC, \\
it follows that $\angle MCA=\angle A$ and $\angle NCB=\angle B$, \\
Hence, $\angle MCN=\angle ACB -\angle MCA-\angle NCB =\angle ACB -(\angle A+\angle B)=\boxed{40^\circ}$.

If $\angle MFN = 70^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle MCN$?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: Given that $MD \perp AC$ and $NE \perp BC$, it follows that $\angle ACB = 180^\circ - \angle MFN = 110^\circ$, which leads to $\angle A + \angle B = 70^\circ$. Given $MA = MC$ and $NB = NC$, it follows that $\angle MCA = \angle A$ and $\angle NCB = \angle B$. Hence, $\angle MCN = \angle ACB - \angle MCA - \angle NCB = \angle ACB - (\angle A + \angle B) = 40^\circ$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is at the lower left, B is at the lower right, C is above; D is located on side AC, E is located on side CB. The line DM passing through D passes through M and extends downward, the line EN passing through E passes through N and extends downward, and the two lines intersect at F below; M and N are located on side AB. The problem gives that DM is the perpendicular bisector of AC, EN is the perpendicular bisector of CB, and ∠MFN=70°. Reasoning: Because DM ⟂ AC and EN ⟂ CB, the angle formed by the lines DM and EN and the angle formed by the lines AC and CB are supplementary angles. From the given ∠MFN=70°, obtain ∠ACB=180°−70°=110°. In triangle ABC, ∠A+∠B=180°−∠ACB=70°. Also because M is on the perpendicular bisector DM of AC, MA=MC, therefore triangle AMC is an isosceles triangle, ∠MCA=∠MAC. From the figure, M is on AB, so ∠MAC is ∠A of triangle ABC, therefore ∠MCA=∠A. Similarly, N is on the perpendicular bisector EN of CB, so NB=NC, therefore triangle CBN is an isosceles triangle, ∠NCB=∠CBN. From the figure, N is on AB, so ∠CBN is ∠B of triangle ABC, therefore ∠NCB=∠B. At point C, ∠MCN=∠ACB−∠MCA−∠NCB=110°−(∠A+∠B)=110°−70°=40°.
